farmer_survey.owner: RESOLVE project team (ESDU, American University of Beirut)
farmer_survey.source: Direct farmer surveys - see instruments chouf_2026 and beqaa_2026
farmer_survey.licence: All rights reserved - research use; contact the RESOLVE team
farmer_survey.consent: Research use only. Public outputs are disclosure-controlled summaries and approximate pins that carry a random ID and farming-practice answers only; names, phone numbers, farm locations, free text and sensitive answers (income, age, gender, costs) are never published.
farmer_survey.method: Answers standardized to controlled vocabularies, resolved to official cadastral units (OCHA COD-AB), and aggregated. A village is published only if at least k respondents answered; otherwise respondents are pooled at district (caza) level. Sensitive indicators (income, age, gender, cost shares) are published at district level only.
caveats: Respondents were not randomly sampled; figures describe respondents, not whole villages.
Pins are placed around the village centre (or the district centre where fewer than k people answered), never at the farm; positions are spread only so each pin can be clicked.
Farmer types and the water-stress / chemical-dependence findings are statistical associations, not causes; see the Insights panel for methods and validation.
Chouf interviews have no recorded dates; Beqaa interviews were on 2026-01-04.
Locations are cadastral areas, never farm or household locations.

fire_detections.source: Most likely NASA FIRMS VIIRS (NOAA-20, Collection 2): an earlier project export of the same format is named fire_archive_J1V-C2. The sensor and query are not recorded in this file.
fire_detections.licence: NASA FIRMS data are free to use with attribution (to be confirmed once the source is re-acquired)
fire_detections.method: Points are the centres of satellite pixels (375 m VIIRS or 1 km MODIS - unknown) flagged as thermal anomalies.
caveats: Not all detections are wildfires; thermal anomalies include agricultural burning and industrial heat.
Detections in South Lebanon rise 4–8× in Sep–Oct 2024, consistent with conflict-related fires.
Confidence and fire radiative power were removed in the legacy file, so low-confidence detections cannot be filtered.
The point marks a pixel centre, not the exact fire location.

protected_areas.owner: UNEP-WCMC / IUCN - World Database on Protected Areas (inferred from field names)
protected_areas.source: Protected Planet WDPA extract; release/version not recorded in the legacy file
protected_areas.licence: WDPA terms of use: attribution required, no commercial use, no redistribution as downloadable data without permission (to be confirmed with UNEP-WCMC)
protected_areas.citation: UNEP-WCMC and IUCN, Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA), www.protectedplanet.net
protected_areas.method: Polygons as published by WDPA; overlapping designations of the same site are kept as separate records.
caveats: Some sites appear more than once because they carry several designations (e.g. national reserve and Ramsar site).
